criteria.evidence: "Out: the project's rule-group record, kept in the product profile beside the setup answers, so the review reads it where every later play reads the project's facts." "Given a rule group that no answer speaks to, when the groups are chosen, then that group is kept." "Writing or changing the rules inside a group (the review's own memory owns them)."

"A group is skipped only when an answer says the project lacks what the group checks; otherwise it is kept. A database group on a project with no database gives only noise, but a group skipped by mistake hides real findings, so only a clear answer can skip one." "Database no: the database group is skipped, because there is no schema, query or data store for its rules to check."

"Given answers that say the project has no permissions, when the rule groups are chosen, then the record marks the permission group as skipped with the permissions answer; given the answer yes, the group is kept." "Surfaces with no web and no mobile: the front-end group is skipped, because there is no screen for its rules to check."

"Which answer decides which group is our default." "Personal data no: the personal-data group is skipped, because the project holds no data about a person for its rules to check. Personal data yes keeps it, and it is never skipped by another answer, because a leak of personal data is the costliest miss."

"A rule group is a set of the review's rules that check one kind of thing (front end, back-end service, database, running service, permissions, personal data); the review runs or skips a group as a whole, so this feature decides per group, never per rule." "Each kept or skipped group names the answer that decided it, so a person can see why a rule did not run." "Running the review and deciding its findings (the review play, /check-change, owns it)."
